text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Building a new nuclear power plant is optional, not obligatory, Finnish Paper Workers Union says, mitigating its demands for more nuclear capacity.
- The era of the welfare state making its citizens passive is over, says Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari, urging changes in the social security system.
- Magnetic encoded strips on old credit and bankcards are too easily forged and should be renewed as soon as possible, a Bank of Finland security manager says.

- Finland's "Young Finns" party cannot support a weak EMU, which the party sees as a reflection of the Western planned economy, party leader Risto E.J. Penttila says explaining the party's change of position.
- Finnish universities and other academic institutions will have up to 25 top-ranking scientific units by the year 2000, Finnish Academy of Scientific Research plans.
- Prices of small apartments in Helsinki fell in May, estate agents say.
- Old-fashioned Russian-built Lada cars do not meet European Union safety regulations, and Finns will be able to buy them for the last time in June before a ban.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finnish forestry industry's competitiveness has improved, making it one of Europe's top elite industries, a study by the European Investment Bank (EIB) shows.
- One-fifth of the motorcycles imported to Finland are brought into the country illegally, eroding the sector's profits and sales, a branch representative says.
- Sharp downward trend in car sales in May suprised the sector completely; Finland's economic outlook would indicate the opposite, a sector representative says.
- Telecom Finland's Internet business director says he expects Finland to pass a new milestone of 700,000 Internet users per week next year.
AAMULEHTI
- Finnish state has negotiated with forestry group Enso ENYRV.HE on the sale of a 300 000 hectare piece of state timberland to Enso.
- Helsinki airport officials fear delays after many air-traffic controllers have left to work in Middle East, lured away by high salaries.
- Democracies should be able to defend their citizens against inner and outer threats, President Ahtisaari says, supporting the idea of banning motorcycle gangs.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Parliament's constitutional affairs committee said a simple majority of MPs could decide the issue of whether Finland is to join the third phase of European economic and monetary union.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
